correctness.rationale: At the exact Padrol–Philippe normalization SP(A)=Σ_{i<j} [−(a_i−a_j)/2,(a_i−a_j)/2], the complex chord identity a_i−a_j=2i exp(πi(i+j)/n) sin(π(i−j)/n) partitions generators into n unoriented directions labelled i+j mod n, at angular gaps π/n. Each class contributes one opposite edge pair of length Σ|a_i−a_j|. For odd n=2m+1, multiplication by 2 acts transitively on the classes and Σ_{d=1}^m 2sin(πd/n)=cot(π/(2n)); the 2n-gon is equilateral and equiangular, hence regular. For even n=2m, the classes split into even and odd sums: total chord lengths 2cot(π/n) and 2csc(π/n). Alternating support numbers p,q obey q−p cos y=cos y and p−q cos y=1, solving p=(1+cos²y)/sin²y and q=2cos y/sin²y. Consecutive support-line intersections have the same radius, proving cyclicity; area=sum h_i L_i/2=n cos y(3+cos²y)/sin³y. Nonidentical alternating lengths imply exactly 2n metric symmetries for even n, versus 4n for regular odd case. Checked raw all-pair chord classes independently for n=3..44; tests supplement all-n trigonometric proof.

final_claim: The canonical centered sweep zonotope of the vertex set of a unit regular n-gon has 2n equally angular edges. It is regular with side length cot(π/(2n)) exactly for odd n; even n yields a cyclic nonregular equiangular 2n-gon with alternating lengths 2cot(π/n),2csc(π/n), exact perimeter and area, and half the full dihedral symmetry order of odd outputs.
